commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace/ref/root bundle

do not infer repository membership or readiness from the filesystem or legacy branch sidecars
commands.note: Status reads workspace, refs, roots, exact tree identity, and semantic counts from one repository authority lease; checkout and Git state are not consulted.

commands.authority: sealed exact-workspace observation consumed by repository-v6 transaction and compare-and-swap ref publication
acceptance_spec: retain a non-fabricable complete workspace observation and its directory capabilities through final authority publication
bind the observed path manifest, exact admission policy, source CAS closure, prior tree, roots, and generation into one commit transaction without replanning against newer authority
reject an unconfirmed mass deletion as a whole observation without publishing simultaneous additions, modifications, policy changes, or graph state
commit exact workspace tree deltas and semantic deltas in one repository transaction
preserve all unsupported-language and non-code artifacts, modes, symlinks, gitlinks, and byte-exact paths
publish the target ref with generation and root-bundle compare-and-swap and no raw-filesystem rebuild
commands.note: Commit consumes one complete host observation that carries the scanner's completion proof into publication, binds the observed manifest to the authority roots and prior workspace tree it was planned against, and refuses rather than replans when authority moved. An unconfirmed mass deletion refuses the whole observation, so no addition, modification, or derived admission-policy state published beside it.

commands.authority: daemon-private repository-v6 exact tree, semantic graph, source CAS, and crash-recoverable projection transaction
acceptance_spec: resolve a selected immutable change through startup-pinned repository and workspace identity without Git or legacy object fallback
refuse a repository storage namespace replaced at the same ambient path, detached, or absent from the pinned store instead of answering from replacement authority
verify complete selected tree, semantic graph, and source CAS closure before one projection and authority transaction

preserve every unsupported-language and non-code artifact, executable bit, symlink, gitlink, opaque binary, and host-unrepresentable byte path in graph authority while materializing only host-representable entries
reject every session-scoped request before mutation and preserve independently dirty unselected paths
replay the exact caller-stable operation across same-daemon and restart crash gaps without advancing authority twice
commands.note: Checkout binds only the repository and workspace identity this daemon pinned at startup, revalidates the retained per-repository storage namespace before planning, and answers a namespace replaced at the same ambient path, detached, or absent from the pinned store with a typed conflict instead of mismatched truth. Exact projection, universal artifact preservation, and caller-stable replay are proven across same-daemon and restart gaps. The retained-identity refusals are proven on Unix; the Windows file-identity path is implemented but not covered by CI.

commands.authority: repository-v6 remote capability and exact transport
acceptance_spec: DONE: negotiate the remote destination lease, build the exact closure, publish it, and verify the returned receipt binds the pack that was sent
DONE: refuse a non-fast-forward gap with both heads named and no force path
OPEN: carry a closure larger than one negotiated envelope (512 changes, 4096 bodies, 16 MiB decoded); transfer v1 has no continuation packs, so a repository past that bound is refused at pack build
OPEN: drive the KinLab control-plane transfer envelope route, including its protection rules and durable receipts, rather than a peer daemon transfer seam directly
commands.note: The full path runs end to end between two Kin daemons over HTTP with receipts verified, but only within one bounded transfer envelope, and the transfer status this protocol publishes still reports push_apply_ready=false. Exposing it as general `kin push` would promise a capability that a repository past the envelope bound does not have.

commands.authority: repository-v6 remote capability and exact transport
acceptance_spec: DONE: read the remote ref advertisement, adopt its default ref when this replica has none, and fetch the exact exported closure
DONE: admit the pack in one local authority transaction and refuse a receipt that does not bind it
DONE: refuse a remote this replica already contains, naming the remote head
OPEN: carry a closure larger than one negotiated envelope; transfer v1 has no continuation packs
OPEN: carry an exported pack past the 24 MiB transfer body bound; the daemon route and the client read declare the same limit, and a pack past it is refused as an oversized envelope rather than split
OPEN: graph-derived workspace transition after admission, so a working tree follows the new head
commands.note: Negotiation, export, and admission run end to end between two Kin daemons over HTTP with receipts verified. It stays closed because the envelope is bounded and because admission does not yet move the workspace to the admitted head. The envelope is bounded twice: by the negotiated change count, and by the 24 MiB one-body transfer bound. A pack carries base64 CAS bodies for the whole source tree, so on a real repository the byte bound binds first.

commands.authority: repository-v6 immutable DAG three-way composition published with ref compare-and-swap
acceptance_spec: resolve both heads and their merge base by replaying the change DAG, never from raw files
compose semantic entities, relations, and exact tree artifacts by stable identity against the merge base
author the merge change against its first parent and record both heads as ordered parents
publish the merge change, the target ref, and the exact workspace in one repository transaction with compare-and-swap
refuse a conflicting, unrelated, criss-cross, or admission-policy-changing merge without publishing any part of it
commands.note: Merge composes graph truth: both heads and the single merge base are materialized by DAG replay, then entities, relations, and exact tree artifacts are merged by stable identity against that base. Composition decides each identity by whole value, so a side that did not move never overrides a side that did, and both sides moving differently is a conflict rather than a resolution. Granularity is the whole entity or artifact, never the line. Two branches editing disjoint regions of one file therefore conflict, because a semantic-entity model has no textual line merge to fall back on. A move on one branch against an edit on the other conflicts as well, because an artifact's path is part of the value being compared and history that records the move as a removal plus an addition leaves the edited side conflicting against that removal. The merge change carries ordered parents with the active branch first and its deltas are authored against that first parent, which is what history replay validates. Up-to-date and fast-forward merges publish no merge change. Unproven shapes fail closed with nothing published and are named in the refusal: conflicting entities, relations, or artifacts, which covers both branches editing one file and a move against an edit; two artifacts composing onto one path; a relation left with no surviving endpoint; unrelated histories; multiple merge bases (criss-cross); a merge that would change the shared admission policy; a dirty or detached workspace. A conflict refusal states the total conflict count, names the first 25 individually, and reports how many further conflicts it found. There is no mid-merge state, so a conflicting merge is refused rather than parked; `kin conflicts` and `kin resolve` stay fail-closed for that reason. One interaction is inherited, not introduced: a workspace whose semantics were installed from history (branch switch, checkout, or merge) and is then committed retains a semantic overlay, because the commit observation re-derives entities from source bytes while the installed ones came from replayed history. `kin branch switch` followed by `kin commit` reproduces it with no merge involved. Until that is fixed, a second merge in the same session refuses on the resulting dirty workspace.

commands.authority: repository-v6 workspace transaction
acceptance_spec: persist and restore exact graph-owned workspace state without branch sidecars or raw-file inference
commands.note: The graph-owned path exists and is covered: sealing writes the exact workspace tree and base-relative semantics as one immutable change under refs/kin/stash/, and restore refuses a moved authority base rather than rebasing onto it. It stays fail-closed because against a live daemon a seal can leave the daemon query graph disagreeing with workspace authority, so the next ready command refuses until the daemon reopens. In-process route coverage does not reproduce it; the background daemon loop is the missing variable.

commands.authority: sealed exact-session observation consumed by repository-v6 explicit ingestion boundary
acceptance_spec: retain the session root capability and a non-fabricable observation seal through final namespace revalidation and authority commit
bind exact policy, exclusions, complete source CAS closure, prior roots, and generation into the consumed observation
reject an unconfirmed mass deletion atomically without admitting simultaneous additions or modifications
admit an explicitly observed projection delta into exact workspace authority with complete artifact identities and source CAS
never answer semantic queries or silently repair authority from raw files
commands.note: The session scanner performs retained-root double observation and authority-root CAS, and its observation now owns the retained no-follow directory capability it was taken through. Every field is private, so the observation cannot be built outside the scanner, and planning re-proves the retained capability before anything is planned against it.

commands.authority: repository-v6 merge transaction state
acceptance_spec: read conflict state committed with the exact merge transaction rather than a .kin sidecar
represent semantic and exact-tree conflicts across every artifact kind
commands.note: Repository-v6 authority has no durable merge-transaction record, so a mid-merge conflict set and its per-entity resolutions cannot be committed with the merge transaction, and the retired sidecar shape (.kin/merge_state.json) is not an acceptable substitute. `kin merge` therefore refuses a conflicting merge atomically instead of parking one, stating the total conflict count and naming the first 25 individually. Flipping this command requires a first-class merge transaction in the kin-model and kin-db substrate.

commands.authority: repository-v6 merge resolution transaction
acceptance_spec: resolve semantic and exact-tree conflicts against one durable merge transaction
publish the resolved workspace and target ref atomically with compare-and-swap
commands.note: Repository-v6 authority has no durable merge-transaction record, so a mid-merge conflict set and its per-entity resolutions cannot be committed with the merge transaction, and the retired sidecar shape (.kin/merge_state.json) is not an acceptable substitute. `kin merge` therefore refuses a conflicting merge atomically instead of parking one, stating the total conflict count and naming the first 25 individually. Flipping this command requires a first-class merge transaction in the kin-model and kin-db substrate.

commands.note: Negotiates against a live peer transfer seam and publishes nothing. Reports whether the gap fits one transfer envelope, because transfer v1 has no continuation packs.
